summary: if runs commands only when a test is true. [ ] (the test command) compares numbers and strings and checks files, and elif and else handle the other cases.
notes: [ "$score" -ge 90 ] compares numbers. For strings use =, as in [ "$letter" = "F" ].
Every if ends with fi, and then goes on the same line as the test after a semicolon: if [ ... ]; then.
Put variables in double quotes inside [ ]. If $name is empty, [ -z "$name" ] still works, but [ -z $name ] can break.
pitfall: Leaving out the spaces breaks the test. ["$score" -ge 90] fails with [92: command not found, because [ is a command and needs spaces around it like any other command.
